job.title: Mid-level Backend Engineer (Python)
must_haves: Comfortable owning a service end-to-end (design, build, deploy, on-call)
Can communicate tradeoffs clearly to non-engineers
nice_to_haves: Exposure to distributed systems / message queues
red_flags: Cannot explain their own past project decisions
Unexplained employment gaps with vague answers

cases.label: clean_strong
cases.cv_summary: 4 yrs backend eng at a logistics startup. Built and owned a Postgres-backed routing service. Led migration from monolith to two services.
cases.interview_notes: Clearly explained the migration decision, tradeoffs of splitting the service, and a specific on-call incident (DB connection pool exhaustion) with root cause. Answers were specific and consistent with CV.
cases.assessment_score: 8/10 take-home: correct solution, clean code, one minor edge case missed.

ground_truth.reasoning: CV, interview, and assessment all corroborate each other. No contradictions.

cases.label: clean_weak
cases.cv_summary: 2 yrs, mostly internal tooling scripts, no production ownership claimed.
cases.interview_notes: Could describe scripts but not how they were deployed or monitored. No on-call experience.
cases.assessment_score: 4/10 take-home: works but has SQL injection vulnerability and no error handling.

ground_truth.reasoning: Below the must-have bar (production ownership) and assessment confirms gaps.

cases.label: conflicting_signals_HARD
cases.cv_summary: CV claims '5 yrs, led a team of 4, owned payments service at [mid-size fintech]' with strong, polished bullet points.
cases.interview_notes: When asked to walk through a specific technical decision on the payments service, answers were vague and generic ('we used best practices', 'the team decided together'). Could not name the database used or describe a single incident. Timeline of the fintech role (14 months per LinkedIn-style record) doesn't match '5 yrs' framing of ownership on CV.
cases.assessment_score: 9/10 take-home: excellent, idiomatic code — notably stronger than the interview performance would suggest, and stylistically inconsistent with the candidate's live-coding notes from the interview.

ground_truth.reasoning: Strong artifacts (CV, take-home) but interview cannot substantiate CV claims, and take-home style doesn't match live coding style — suggests possible take-home assistance or CV inflation. This is the case a naive system would wrongly advance because two of three signals look excellent.

cases.label: clean_strong
cases.cv_summary: 3.5 yrs, owned a FastAPI service with async job queue, has on-call rotation experience.
cases.interview_notes: Explained async/await tradeoffs correctly, described a real deadlock bug and fix. Consistent with CV.

ground_truth.reasoning: Consistent, meets must-haves and some nice-to-haves.

cases.label: gap_explained
cases.interview_notes: Explained gap clearly as a family medical leave, returned with a personal project (documented on GitHub) demonstrating continued skill.

ground_truth.reasoning: Gap is explained and substantiated; not a genuine red flag despite matching the JD's red-flag keyword.

cases.label: gap_unexplained
cases.cv_summary: 3 yrs experience, two unexplained 6+ month gaps.
cases.interview_notes: Vague, evasive answers about the gaps ('personal reasons', declined to elaborate twice when asked directly about work during those periods).

ground_truth.reasoning: Matches JD's explicit red flag; evasiveness (not the gap itself) is the actual signal.

cases.label: clean_weak
cases.cv_summary: 6 yrs experience but entirely in a different stack (embedded C), no Python production work.
cases.interview_notes: Strong engineer, clearly experienced, but admits limited Python exposure ('learning it now').
cases.assessment_score: 5/10: functional but non-idiomatic Python, clearly a non-native Python speaker.

ground_truth.reasoning: Doesn't meet the specific must-have (3+ yrs production Python) despite general seniority.

cases.label: nice_to_have_boost
cases.cv_summary: 3 yrs Python, Postgres, plus 1.5 yrs at a Series A startup with distributed systems (Kafka) exposure.
cases.interview_notes: Clear, specific answers about a Kafka consumer-lag incident. Consistent with CV.

ground_truth.reasoning: Meets must-haves and several nice-to-haves, fully corroborated.

cases.label: conflicting_signals_moderate
cases.cv_summary: CV states 'expert in FastAPI and asyncio', listed as a core skill at the top.
cases.interview_notes: When asked a basic asyncio question (difference between concurrency and parallelism in Python's GIL context), gave an incorrect answer and could not self-correct when prompted.
cases.assessment_score: 6/10: take-home used Flask, not FastAPI, despite FastAPI being listed as their tool of choice.

ground_truth.reasoning: A stated 'expert' skill is contradicted by both the interview and the candidate's own tool choice on the take-home.

cases.label: clean_strong
cases.cv_summary: 4 yrs, owned two services end-to-end at a B2B SaaS company, mentored two juniors.
cases.interview_notes: Explained a specific tradeoff decision (denormalizing a table for read performance) with clear reasoning about when they'd reverse it. Communicated clearly, translated technical tradeoff into business impact.

ground_truth.reasoning: Strong on both the must-have technical bar and the communication must-have.

cases.label: clean_weak_confident
cases.cv_summary: CV is extremely polished, uses strong action verbs and metrics ('improved performance by 300%') but metrics are unexplained.
cases.interview_notes: Could not explain how the 300% figure was measured or what the baseline was. Vague on methodology when pressed twice.

ground_truth.reasoning: Unsubstantiated metrics plus a weak assessment; CV polish alone is not evidence.

cases.label: conflicting_signals_moderate
cases.cv_summary: CV claims sole ownership of a well-known open-source-adjacent internal tool.
cases.interview_notes: Described the tool accurately and in detail, but repeatedly used 'we' language and, when asked directly 'what part did you personally write', named only a small config module; the rest was attributed to 'the team'.

ground_truth.reasoning: Scope of ownership on CV ('sole ownership') is contradicted by the candidate's own interview language once probed.
